standard.title: Create and present texts for purpose and audience
standard.description: create and present informative and imaginative spoken, written and multimodal texts, appropriate to purpose and audience, using a range of sentence structures to sequence information and ideas, and textual conventions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can create and present a range of informative and imaginative texts using sentence structures and textual conventions (AC9LCH4C05). They can perform and present to real audiences. They have not yet deliberately adapted texts for different purposes and audiences, used complex sentence structures to sequence information cohesively, or produced community-facing content for external audiences.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create and present informative and imaginative texts appropriate to purpose and audience, using a range of sentence structures to sequence and develop information and ideas with textual coherence.

nodes.label: Sequencing and cohesion in extended texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can sequence information and ideas in extended texts using cohesive devices — connectives, discourse markers, time expressions — to create coherent and fluent written or spoken texts.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a text of at least eight target language sentences using at least three different cohesive devices to connect ideas.
nodes.typical_width: Use a range of cohesive devices — sequence words, conjunctions, temporal and logical connectives — to organise and sequence information across a text; build more complex messages using joining words and sequence markers; apply appropriate punctuation for text-level coherence.
wider: Analyse the cohesive devices used in a model text and then reproduce the same organisational pattern with original content — compare the effect of the pattern with and without cohesive devices
Compare how cohesion is achieved in the target language with English — identify where the devices are similar (equivalent connectives) and where the languages handle sequencing differently
nodes.hinge_reason: Cohesion and sequencing are the prerequisites for extended text production. Students who can only produce isolated sentences cannot create the informative or imaginative texts with developed ideas that this descriptor requires.

response_modes.reason: Cohesive device use requires repeated practice across text types before it becomes reliable. Explicit modelling followed by scaffolded production — with progressive removal of structural support — builds the fluency that produces cohesive extended texts.

success_criteria: Produces a text of at least eight sentences using at least three cohesive devices
The text has clear logical or temporal sequencing that can be followed by a reader

nodes.label: Adapting texts for purpose and audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can adapt language register, content and format deliberately to suit a specific purpose and audience when creating a text.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a text with at least two deliberate adaptations for a specific purpose or audience — for example, formal language for an adult audience, simplified language for younger students, or persuasive language for a campaign.
nodes.typical_width: Create informative and imaginative texts adapted for different purposes and audiences — community newsletters, travel brochures, procedures, advertisements, stories; select vocabulary, register and format appropriate to the audience; support content with visual elements where appropriate.
wider: Create the same content in two different formats for two different audiences — compare the language and format choices made and explain how each serves its intended audience

Research and adopt the conventions of a specific real-world text type (e.g. a formal report, a digital advertisement) in the target language and produce a text that authentically follows those conventions

response_modes.reason: Audience and purpose adaptation requires students to make deliberate, reasoned language choices — not default to familiar patterns. Explicit audience analysis before drafting — who is this for? what do they need? — builds the planning capacity that underlies purposeful text creation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Audience-aware text creation is the clearest marker of communicative maturity at Y5-6. Width investment here — particularly in real community-facing audiences — creates genuine communicative purpose and produces the highest-quality creative output.
success_criteria: Creates a text with at least two deliberate language or format adaptations appropriate to purpose or audience
Can explain the choices made and why they suit the specified audience

nodes.label: Creating and performing imaginative texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create and perform imaginative texts — plays, stories, scripts, poems — that demonstrate language choice, structural creativity and personal voice.
nodes.minimum_width: Create and perform an imaginative text demonstrating at least one creative language choice (figurative language, wordplay, structural variation, or descriptive language) and at least one deliberate structural decision.
nodes.typical_width: Create and perform imaginative texts — scripted plays, stories, modified folk tales, imagined interactions, letters to future self — using descriptive language, experimenting with structure, and demonstrating personal voice; share creative work with appropriate audiences.
wider: Create an original imaginative text in the target language with a deliberate creative vision — explain the structural and language choices made and how they serve the creative purpose
Write for a future reader — for example, a letter to themselves at graduation — using appropriate language and structure for the purpose, then compare with a peer's version

response_modes.reason: Imaginative text creation integrates cohesion skills (node 1) and audience-aware adaptation (node 2) in a creative register where personal expression is the primary purpose. The teaching investment is in creating genuine creative freedom within structural parameters — students decide what to express, the framework helps them shape it.

success_criteria: Creates an imaginative text demonstrating at least one creative language choice and at least one deliberate structural decision
Performs or presents the text demonstrating awareness of audience through delivery
